st.1: The name "Sindhu-Sarasvati Civilisation" stresses the sites on the Ravi–Beas system.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the name stresses the sites on the Ghaggar–Hakra (Sarasvati) system. Statement 3 is wrong: the term "Indus Valley Civilisation" was coined by John Marshall.

st.1: Harappa lies in Sahiwal (Montgomery) district of Punjab, on the left bank of the Ravi.

x: All three statements are correct: Harappa is on the left bank of the Ravi, Mohenjodaro on the right bank of the Indus, and Chanhudaro about 130 km south of Mohenjodaro.

st.1: A woven jute piece was found at Mohenjodaro.
st.4: Millets and rice were staples at Mohenjodaro and Harappa.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the woven piece found at Mohenjodaro was of cotton. Statement 2 is wrong: the earliest rice (husk) comes from Lothal and Rangpur, not Chanhudaro. Statement 4 is wrong: millets and rice were staples at Rangpur and Surkotada; wheat and barley were the staples at Mohenjodaro and Harappa.

st.3: No temple has been clearly identified at any Harappan site.

x: All three statements are correct: religion was present but not dominant, worship was nature- and fertility-oriented, and no clear temple has been identified.

st.3: Hastinapur in Meerut district was a capital of the Panchala kingdom.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Kurus held the upper Doab around Kurukshetra; the Panchalas held the middle Doab (Bareilly–Badaun–Farrukhabad). Statement 3 is wrong: Hastinapur was a capital of the Kurus, not the Panchalas.

st.4: Sanghabhuti, a monk in Sri Lanka (381–384 CE), wrote a commentary on the Sarvastivada Vinaya.
st.2: Buddhaghosa was a 5th-century Mahayana scholar.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Buddhaghosa was a Theravada scholar. Statement 3 is wrong: Ashvaghosha lived at the court of Kanishka. Statement 4 is wrong: Sanghabhuti worked in China, not Sri Lanka.

st.4: The doctrine of niyati (fate) belongs to the Jains, not to the Ajivikas.
st.1: Kundakundacharya, a Svetambara monk, wrote the Samayasara and Pravachanasara.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Kundakundacharya was a Digambara monk. Statement 3 is wrong: the Yogasara is not Kundakunda's work (APPSC keys it to Nagarjuna). Statement 4 is wrong: niyati is the Ajivika doctrine of Makkhali Gosala, not a Jain one.

st.1: Pillar Edict IV gave the dharma-mahamatras independent judicial power in the 26th regnal year.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Pillar Edict IV gave this power to the rajukas. Statement 4 is wrong: Rock Edict II extends its welfare measures beyond the empire to the Tamil lands (Cholas, Pandyas, Satiyaputras, Keralaputras).

st.2: Kantakashodhana courts were presided over by three pradeshtris.

x: All three statements are correct: Dharmasthiya (civil) courts had three dharmasthas, Kantakashodhana (criminal) courts had three pradeshtris, and the Pradvivaka was the chief judge.

st.2: Heliodorus, who set up the Garuda pillar at Besnagar, was the envoy of the Indo-Greek king Antialcidas.

x: All three statements are correct: Bhagavatism centred on Vasudeva-Krishna, and Heliodorus was the envoy of Antialcidas of Taxila at the court of the Sunga king Bhagabhadra.

st.3: The Narada Smriti is one of the law books of the Mauryan age.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Jayadeva was the court poet of the Sena king Lakshmana Sena, not the Pala Dharmapala. Statement 3 is wrong: the Narada Smriti is a law book of the Gupta age.

st.2: Bagh has nine Jain viharas.
st.3: The Udayagiri group near Vidisha has 12 caves.
st.1: The Bagh caves lie in Raisen district on the Baghani river.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Bagh caves are in Dhar district. Statement 2 is wrong: Bagh's nine viharas are Buddhist. Statement 3 is wrong: the Udayagiri group has 20 caves. Statement 4 is wrong: Virasena's Udayagiri inscription records Chandragupta II, not Samudragupta.

st.1: The Prayag assembly was held once every ten years.
st.3: The Kannauj assembly lasted 75 days.
st.4: Hiuen Tsang attended the fifth Prayag assembly.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Prayag assembly was held every five years. Statement 2 is wrong: the Maha Moksha Parishad met at Prayag. Statement 3 is wrong: the Kannauj assembly lasted 23 days (75 days was the Prayag assembly). Statement 4 is wrong: Hiuen Tsang attended the sixth Prayag assembly.

st.4: Matanga Divakara was a court poet of Bhaskaravarman.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Bana was a native of Pritikuta on the Sone (Hiranyavahu), not the Narmada. Statement 4 is wrong: Matanga Divakara was a court poet of Harsha.

st.3: The Bahmani kingdom was founded only later, in 1347.

x: All three statements are correct: 1336 saw the founding of Vijayanagara and Kapaya Nayaka's recapture of Warangal, while the Bahmani kingdom came in 1347.

st.4: War elephants were kept mainly by the iqtadars, not by the Sultan.
st.1: Alauddin Khalji set up the Diwan-i-Arz under the Ariz-i-Mumalik to keep a large standing army against the Mongols.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Diwan-i-Arz was set up by Balban. Statement 2 is wrong: horses were mainly imported from Central Asia and Arabia, not Bengal. Statement 4 is wrong: war elephants were a monopoly of the Sultan.

st.1: Both Ziauddin Barani and Minhaj-us-Siraj wrote works with this title.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the two authors of a Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi are Barani and Shams Siraj Afif (Minhaj wrote the Tabaqat-i-Nasiri). Statement 2 is wrong: Afif's work covers the reign of Firoz Shah Tughlaq, not Balban.

st.1: Arabic was the official language of the Delhi Sultanate, while Persian was the religious language.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Persian was the official language and Arabic the religious one. Statement 2 is wrong: the Mahabharata and the Rajatarangini were rendered into Persian under Akbar, not Firoz Tughlaq.

st.2: Badan Singh founded the Jat state of Alwar in 1722.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Guru Ghasidas belongs to the 19th century; the 1672 revolt was of the Satnamis of Narnaul. Statement 2 is wrong: Badan Singh founded the Jat state of Bharatpur, not Alwar.

st.2: Saadat Khan Burhan-ul-Mulk founded the Awadh state.

x: All three statements are correct: Murshid Quli Khan founded Bengal, Saadat Khan Burhan-ul-Mulk founded Awadh, and Nizam-ul-Mulk became autonomous after Shakarkheda (1724).

st.1: He defeated the Mughal governor Mubariz Khan at Shakar Kheda in 1720.
st.2: He had been Subedar of Bengal and Mughal Wazir before he left for the Deccan.

x: Statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Shakar Kheda was fought in 1724. Statement 2 is wrong: he had been Subedar of the Deccan, not Bengal. Statement 3 is wrong: the title Nizam-ul-Mulk was conferred by Farrukhsiyar.

st.3: It was founded by the French in 1723.

x: All three statements are correct: Yanam, the only French territory in Andhra, was founded in 1723 and stayed French until 1954.

st.1: Sambalpur was annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse in 1852.
st.3: The British refused to recognise Nana Saheb, the adopted son of Rani Lakshmibai.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Sambalpur was annexed in 1849. Statement 3 is wrong: Rani Lakshmibai's adopted son was Damodar Rao (Nana Saheb was the adopted son of Baji Rao II). Statement 4 is wrong: Jaipur was never annexed (it was Jaitpur).

st.3: Bentinck introduced the Mahalwari settlement by Regulation VII of 1822.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Mahalwari began under Regulation VII of 1822 (Holt Mackenzie); Bentinck revised it by Regulation IX of 1833. Statement 4 is wrong: slavery was abolished in 1843 under Ellenborough.

st.3: He was the first Indian elected to the House of Commons, from Holborn in 1892.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: he was elected from Finsbury Central (he had lost at Holborn in 1886). Statement 4 is wrong: he declared Swaraj the goal at the Calcutta Congress of 1906.

st.1: The Hunter Commission (1902) led to the Indian Universities Act, 1904, which increased government control over universities.
st.2: The Hartog Committee recommended a twelve-year school course, an intermediate stage and a three-year degree.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 1902 body was the Raleigh Commission. Statement 2 is wrong: these were the Sadler Commission's recommendations. Statement 3 is wrong: Ashutosh Mukherjee was a member of the Sadler Commission, not the Hartog Committee.

st.2: On repeal, the pre-censorship clause was retained and a press commissioner was appointed.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the pre-censorship clause was dropped. Statement 4 is wrong: Section 124A was added in 1870 under Lord Mayo.

st.4: Muslims were given seats strictly in proportion to their population share.
st.3: Additional members of the Central Council were raised to 60, and a non-official majority was introduced there.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: members could discuss the budget and move resolutions but could not vote on it as a whole. Statement 3 is wrong: an official majority was kept at the Centre (non-official majorities came only in the provinces). Statement 4 is wrong: Muslims got more seats than their population share.

st.1: The Montagu Declaration of 20 August 1918 promised the progressive realisation of responsible government in India as an integral part of the British Empire.
st.4: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report came out in 1919.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Declaration was made on 20 August 1917. Statement 2 is wrong: the pressure came from the Home Rule movement (the Swaraj Party came only in 1923). Statement 4 is wrong: the Report came out in 1918.

st.1: He was born in 1827 at Satara in the Mahar community.
st.2: The title 'Mahatma' was given to him in 1873 by Vithalrao Krishnaji Vandekar.

x: Statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Phule belonged to the Mali community. Statement 2 is wrong: the title 'Mahatma' came in 1888. Statement 3 is wrong: his 1848 girls' school was at Pune, not Bombay.

st.2: At the Adi Andhra Mahasabha of 1936, Kusuma Dharmanna urged socialism.

x: All three statements are correct: Chilukuri Venkataswamy presided in 1919, Kusuma Dharmanna urged socialism at Vizianagaram in 1936, and the 1917 resolution sought 'Adi Hindu' and 'Adi Andhra' in place of 'Panchama'.

st.4: It reserved 3% of seats for women in all provinces, including the NWFP.
st.3: The depressed classes got only a separate electorate, with no vote in the general electorate.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it followed the failure of the Second Round Table Conference. Statement 3 is wrong: the depressed classes got a double vote, in a separate and in the general electorate. Statement 4 is wrong: the NWFP was left out of the 3% reservation for women.

st.3: His guru was Swami Virajananda of Varanasi.
st.2: He was born in a Brahmin family at Porbandar, Gujarat.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: he was born at Tankara in Morvi state. Statement 3 is wrong: Virajananda was of Mathura. Statement 4 is wrong: he died at Ajmer in 1883.

st.2: He rejected the authority of the Puranas and accepted only the Vedas.

x: All three statements are correct: he held the Vedas infallible, rejected the Puranas and held that caste should depend on merit and occupation.

st.2: She started the Home Rule League on 28 April 1916.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Besant started her League on 1 September 1916 (28 April 1916 was Tilak's League). Statement 3 is wrong: she presided over the Calcutta session of 1917.

st.3: 'History of the Indian National Congress' was written by Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

x: All three statements are correct: Anandacharlu attended the first session in 1885 and presided at Nagpur in 1891, and Pattabhi Sitaramayya wrote the History of the INC.

st.2: The first principal of the Bengal National College was Aurobindo Ghosh.

x: All three statements are correct: the National Council of Education grew into Jadavpur University, Aurobindo Ghosh was the first principal of the Bengal National College, and the Calcutta Congress of 1906 declared Swaraj the goal.

st.1: It was Gandhi's first hunger strike in India – he fasted against the indigo planters.
st.2: It followed the Kheda Satyagraha and preceded the Ahmedabad mill strike.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Champaran was the first civil disobedience (his first fast came in the Ahmedabad mill strike of 1918). Statement 2 is wrong: Champaran (1917) came before Kheda (1918). Statement 3 is wrong: satyagraha was first formulated in South Africa.

st.1: The Congress Working Committee accepted it at Allahabad on 14 July 1942.
st.3: It was moved by Sardar Patel and seconded by Jawaharlal Nehru.

x: Statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the CWC accepted it at Wardha. Statement 2 is wrong: the AICC ratified it on 8 August 1942. Statement 3 is wrong: it was moved by Nehru and seconded by Patel.

st.2: On 20 February 1947 Attlee declared that the British would leave India by August 1947.
st.3: The Royal Indian Navy was set up in 1939.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Attlee's deadline was June 1948. Statement 3 is wrong: the RIN was set up in 1934. Statement 4 is wrong: the ratings got freedom-fighter pensions in 1973.

st.1: When Hyderabad State was dissolved on 1 November 1956, Marathwada went to Bombay State.

x: All three statements are correct: Marathwada went to Bombay State, the 7th Amendment ended Part B states and Rajpramukhs, and the 26th Amendment abolished privy purses.

st.1: Nyapati Subba Rao presided over the first session.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the first session (Bapatla 1913) was presided over by B.N. Sarma; Nyapati Subba Rao presided over the second. Statement 2 is wrong: the third session (Visakhapatnam 1915) was presided over by the Raja of Panagal.

st.3: The Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission was set up in 1953.
st.2: Andhra Pradesh, formed under Section 3 of the Act, was the first linguistic state of independent India.
st.1: The States Reorganisation Act came into force on 1 October 1956.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Act came into force on 1 November 1956. Statement 2 is wrong: the first linguistic state was Andhra State (1953); AP was the first state formed under the SR Act. Statement 3 is wrong: the APPSC was set up in 1956. Statement 4 is wrong: the Act created 14 states and 6 Union Territories.

st.1: He founded the Andhra Mahasabha.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: he founded and led the Hyderabad State Congress, not the Andhra Mahasabha. Statement 2 is wrong: at the 1954 Mahasabha he strongly supported Visalandhra.

st.2: The draft Bill named the State "Andhra Telangana"; the Communists wanted "Visalandhra"; the States Reorganisation Commission chose "Andhra Pradesh".
st.1: It joined the 11 districts of Andhra State with 8 Telugu districts of Hyderabad State.
st.4: Kurnool was kept as the capital in view of the SRC's opinion and the Mahasabha demand.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: nine Telugu districts of Hyderabad State joined. Statement 2 is wrong: the Joint Select Committee chose the name "Andhra Pradesh". Statement 3 is wrong: the Andhra Legislature backed the merger unanimously. Statement 4 is wrong: Hyderabad was made the capital.

st.1: Jonnawada, a megalithic site, is in Kurnool district.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Jonnawada is in Nellore district. Statement 3 is wrong: the Mayiladumparai dates make the South Indian Iron Age earlier than the Gangetic one.

st.2: E.J. Rapson placed their origin in the western Deccan (Maharashtra) from the Puranic 'Andhra' names.
st.3: K.A. Nilakanta Sastri took 'Andhra' as dynastic, 'Satavahana' as tribal and 'Satakarni' as a family name.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Rapson placed their origin in the eastern Deccan (Andhra). Statement 3 is wrong: Sastri took 'Andhra' as tribal and 'Satavahana' as dynastic. Statement 4 is wrong: Bhandarkar held that the Andhras and the Satavahanas were the same.

st.4: The Kanhabenna of the Hathigumpha inscription is the Godavari river.
st.2: The Chulakalinga Jataka is a Jain text that records the contact between Kalinga and the Satavahanas.
st.1: Early Satavahana history is told in the Mudrarakshasa and the Dvatrimsatputtalika.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the literary sources are the Kathasaritsagara and the Dvatrimsatputtalika. Statement 2 is wrong: the Chulakalinga Jataka is a Buddhist text. Statement 3 is wrong: Kharavela only sent his army west disregarding Satakarni; no defeat is recorded. Statement 4 is wrong: the Kanhabenna is the Krishna.

st.1: The Raja was the highest feudatory but could not issue coins.
st.2: The Maharathis were hereditary tax-collecting feudatories mainly of the eastern Deccan.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Raja could issue coins. Statement 2 is wrong: the Maharathis were mainly of the western Deccan. Statement 4 is wrong: the Raja ranked above the Mahabhoja.

st.1: Bhaga, the king's share of one-fourth of the produce, was the chief income.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: bhaga was one-sixth of the produce. Statement 3 is wrong: royal officers were barred from entering granted land.

st.1: Unlike Gandhara, it shows no Greco-Roman influence.

x: All three statements are correct: the Amaravati school was indigenous, spread to Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia, and reached its final phase under the Ikshvakus.

st.3: Under the Vishnukundins, farmers were regarded as 'the backbone' of society and received land grants.

x: All three statements are correct: the Nanaghat inscription refers to Vedic Brahmins, Dakshamitra shows foreigners taking Indian names, and under the Vishnukundins farmers were 'the backbone'.

st.1: Bodhisri built a stone mandapa at the eastern gateway of the Maha Chaitya at Amaravati.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: her stone mandapa was at Kantakasala (Ghantasala). Statement 2 is wrong: her seven viharas were at Papili, not Salihundam.

st.3: Special Ghatikas functioned at Nagarjunakonda and Ghantasala.
st.1: They were higher colleges of Prakrit and Buddhist learning.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Ghatikas were colleges of Sanskrit and Vedic learning. Statement 3 is wrong: special Ghatikas were at Amaravati and Vengi. Statement 4 is wrong: they taught 14 vidyas (4 Vedas, 6 Vedangas, Mimamsa, Nyaya, Dharmashastra, Puranas).

st.1: The Eastern Chalukya king Vishnuvardhana is credited with the Undavalli, Bhairavakonda and Mogalrajapuram caves.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: these caves are credited to the Vishnukundin Madhava Varma I. Statement 3 is wrong: the Udayagiri caves of Madhya Pradesh are associated with the Guptas.

st.1: The Mahabalipuram monuments were inscribed on the UNESCO list in 1986.
st.3: Ajanta consists of 25 chaityas and 4 viharas.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Mahabalipuram was inscribed in 1984. Statement 3 is wrong: Ajanta has 25 viharas and 4 chaityas. Statement 4 is wrong: the caves were found in 1819 by John Smith.

st.3: The Kayasthas revolted under Jannigadeva (1272) with Pandya support.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: in Rayalaseema Vijayanagara succeeded the Kakatiyas. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1272 Kayastha revolt was led by Ambadeva.

st.3: Ibrahim Lodi conquered Jaunpur in 1479.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Bengal was annexed in 1576. Statement 3 is wrong: Jaunpur was conquered by Bahlul Lodi.

st.1: The Qutb Shahis united the Telugu lands for the third time, after the Satavahanas and the Kakatiyas.

x: All three statements are correct: the Qutb Shahis were the third to unite the Telugu lands (after the Satavahanas and Kakatiyas), Muharram became Peerla Panduga, and Bonalu began at the Golconda Mahankali temple.

st.2: Robert Sewell backed the Kannada (Hoysala) theory.
st.4: P.B. Desai backed the Andhra theory.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Sewell backed the Andhra theory. Statement 3 is wrong: Nilakanta Sastri backed the Andhra theory. Statement 4 is wrong: P.B. Desai backed the Kannada theory (N. Venkataramanayya backed the Andhra theory).

st.2: The Padmakshi temple at Hanumakonda, built by Prola II, was originally a Buddhist shrine.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Padmakshi temple was originally a Jain shrine. Statement 3 is wrong: the Kadalalaya basadi was built by Mailama, wife of the minister Bethana, not by a queen.

st.1: Kanyashulkam meant dowry.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: kanyashulkam meant bride price. Statement 2 is wrong: varashulkam meant dowry (groom price), not slavery.

st.2: His Telugu Grammar (1840) came before his Telugu-English and English-Telugu dictionaries.

x: All three statements are correct: Brown learnt Telugu from Kodandarama Pantulu, his Grammar (1840) preceded his dictionaries, and he preserved Mackenzie's Kaifiyats.

st.3: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham co-organised the students' protest with Gadicherla.
st.2: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao defied the authorities by presenting an address to Lala Lajpat Rai.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Gadicherla presented the address to Bipin Chandra Pal. Statement 3 is wrong: he organised the protest with J. Ramachandra Rao (Chilakamarti translated Pal's speech). Statement 4 is wrong: 138 students were debarred for two years.

st.1: It was observed in 1923 at Calcutta.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the first Labour Day was observed at Madras in 1923. Statement 2 is wrong: it was organised by Singaravelu's Labour Kisan Party of Hindustan, not the Forward Bloc.

st.3: It came into force on 26 January 1950.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: zamindars were paid compensation. Statement 3 is wrong: the Act came into force on 7 September 1949.

st.3: The Palemkota revolt broke out there on 20 March 1931.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: kancha paddhati was the yearly auction of grazing land. Statement 3 is wrong: the Palemkota revolt broke out on 20 March 1933.

st.3: The paper Prajavani was edited by N.G. Ranga.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Zamin Rytu was started by Nellore Venkatarama Naidu. Statement 3 is wrong: Prajavani was edited by Garimella Krishnamurthy.

st.3: It was led on the ground by Vennelakanti Raghavaiah.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: it was led on the ground by Kommareddi Satyanarayana. Statement 4 is wrong: the memorandum went to Speaker Bulusu Sambamurthy, not Prakasam.

st.1: Adibhatla Narayana Dasu bears the title Burrakatha Pitamaha.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Adibhatla Narayana Dasu is the Harikatha Pitamaha. Statement 2 is wrong: Sheikh Nazar is the Burrakatha Pitamaha.

st.2: Tarangam, dancing on the rim of a brass plate, is a feature of Kuchipudi and not of Bharatanatyam.

x: All three statements are correct: Kuchipudi is named after its Krishna district village, Tarangam is a Kuchipudi feature, and Kuchipudi grew as dance-drama while Bharatanatyam was solo temple dance.

st.2: It is given in 22 languages.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it is given in 24 languages. Statement 3 is wrong: besides the 22 Eighth Schedule languages it covers English and Rajasthani (Sindhi is already in the Eighth Schedule).

st.2: Diodotus founded the Graeco-Bactrian kingdom by revolting against the Seleucids.

x: All three statements are correct: Gedrosia is Balochistan, Diodotus revolted against the Seleucids, and Demetrius was the first Bactrian Greek to invade India.

st.2: The Gwalior inscription says Dantidurga crushed the mleccha (Arab) army.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Gwalior inscription credits the Pratihara Nagabhata I. Statement 3 is wrong: Arab rule stayed confined to Sindh (and Multan).

st.3: The Narthamalai paintings depict Shiva and Parvati.

x: All three statements are correct: the Brihadeeswara frescoes show Shiva as Tripurantaka and Rajaraja I with Karuvur Thevar, and Narthamalai shows Shiva and Parvati.

st.3: The vimana of the Gangaikondacholapuram temple is about 180 ft high, with a straight pyramidal profile.
st.2: Its granite vimana is about 216 ft high, with a capstone of about 20 tonnes.
st.1: The Airavatesvara temple at Darasuram is also called Dakshina Meru.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Dakshina Meru is the Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur. Statement 2 is wrong: its capstone weighs about 80 tonnes. Statement 3 is wrong: the Gangaikondacholapuram vimana has a concave curvilinear profile. Statement 4 is wrong: the musical steps and stone chariot belong to the Airavatesvara temple, Darasuram.

st.2: Al-Biruni was the poet laureate (Malik-ush-Shuara).

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the poet laureate was Unsuri. Statement 3 is wrong: Kitab-ul-Hind was translated into English by Edward Sachau.

st.1: The family protects only its earning members from social and economic risks.
st.4: Persistent failure of family functions, as through abuse or alcoholism, is called role conflict.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the family protects all its members, not only earners. Statement 3 is wrong: inheritance is the passing of property and status across generations, not collective consumption. Statement 4 is wrong: such persistent failure is called dysfunction.

st.4: According to the OECD, India will have the world's largest middle class by 2025.
st.1: NCAER defines the middle class as those earning $10-50 a day (PPP).

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the $10-50 a day definition is the World Bank's (NCAER uses ₹2-10 lakh a year). Statement 3 is wrong: it is projected to reach 61% by 2047. Statement 4 is wrong: the OECD year is 2035.

st.3: A first breach involving hazardous sewer cleaning is punishable with up to 2 years and/or ₹5 lakh.
st.2: A first breach is punishable with up to 1 year and/or ₹1 lakh.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: implementation is monitored by the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis. Statement 2 is wrong: the fine for a first breach is up to ₹50,000. Statement 3 is wrong: the fine for a first hazardous-cleaning breach is up to ₹2 lakh.

st.2: Article 51A(f) asks citizens to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: this duty is in Article 51A(e). Statement 4 is wrong: the Places of Worship Act freezes the character as on 15 August 1947.

st.1: Its full name is the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Punishment) Act, 2013.
st.2: An Internal Committee is presided over by a senior woman employee, has one NGO member and at least one-third of its members are women.

x: Statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the last word of the title is 'Redressal'. Statement 2 is wrong: at least half the Internal Committee members must be women. Statement 3 is wrong: the Local Committee is constituted by the District Officer.

st.4: It recommended raising the age of consent to 18, but Parliament kept it at 16.
st.2: It recommended retaining the marital rape exception.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it recommended criminalising marital rape. Statement 3 is wrong: it did not recommend the death penalty for rape. Statement 4 is wrong: it recommended keeping the age of consent at 16, and Parliament fixed it at 18.

st.4: The JJ Act, 2015 made registration compulsory only for government-run Child Care Institutions.
st.1: A Juvenile Justice Board has a Principal Magistrate and two social workers, both of whom must be women.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: only at least one of the two social workers must be a woman. Statement 3 is wrong: working children are children in need of care and protection. Statement 4 is wrong: registration is compulsory for all Child Care Institutions.

st.3: The concept of 'street-level bureaucracy' was given by Michael Lipsky.

x: All three statements are correct: Hood's NATO tools, Pressman and Wildavsky's top-down study, and Lipsky's 'street-level bureaucracy'.

st.2: The Prime Minister's Office is headed by the Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister.

x: All three statements are correct: the Cabinet Secretariat works under the PM, the PMO is headed by the Principal Secretary, and NITI Aayog is a non-statutory body chaired by the PM.

st.2: If work is not provided within 30 days of demand, an unemployment allowance is due.
st.1: It guarantees at least 100 days of wage work in a financial year to every rural adult.

x: Statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the guarantee is per rural household, not per adult. Statement 2 is wrong: the allowance is due if work is not given within 15 days. Statement 3 is wrong: at least one-third of the workers must be women.

st.3: Palna, the National Creche Scheme, is meant for children of 6 months–6 years, whether or not the mother is employed.

x: All three statements are correct: PM CARES gives ₹10 lakh at 23, the 2021 Amendment made the DM the focal point for adoption, and Palna covers children of 6 months–6 years.

st.4: The National Policy for Senior Citizens, 2011 focuses on institutional care in old-age homes.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the NPHCE is run by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. Statement 4 is wrong: the 2011 policy focuses on 'ageing in place', not institutional care.

st.1: The Rights of Transgender Persons Bill, 2014 was a government Bill moved by Tiruchi Siva.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: it was a private member's Bill. Statement 2 is wrong: it was passed only by the Rajya Sabha (2015).

st.2: SBM-Gramin Phase II targets garbage-free villages, while SBM-Urban 2.0 targets ODF Plus cities.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: SBM-G Phase II targets ODF Plus villages and SBM-U 2.0 targets garbage-free cities. Statement 3 is wrong: the India Sanitation Coalition was set up by FICCI.

st.2: SHANTI is to be operationalised first in the Bay of Bengal.

x: All three statements are correct: SAGAR casts India as a net security provider, SHANTI starts in the Bay of Bengal, and the Colombo Security Conclave began in 2011 as an India–Sri Lanka–Maldives trilateral.

st.1: Dr Harsh Vardhan chaired the World Health Assembly in 2020-21.
st.2: Apurva Chandra chaired the International Labour Conference in 2020-21.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Harsh Vardhan chaired the WHO Executive Board. Statement 2 is wrong: Apurva Chandra chaired the ILO Governing Body. Statement 3 is wrong: in March 2025 India chaired the Commission on Narcotic Drugs, not UNODC.

st.3: It is headquartered at Shanghai and its Indian regional office is at GIFT City, Gandhinagar.

x: All three statements are correct: the NDB was mooted at New Delhi (2012), agreed at Fortaleza (2014), and has its HQ in Shanghai with an Indian regional office at GIFT City.

st.2: India amended its Patents Act to allow product patents in 2005.

x: All three statements are correct: the GI Act came in 1999, product patents in 2005, and the first compulsory licence in 2012 (Natco-Bayer).

st.3: The Dunkel Draft (1991) belonged to the Uruguay Round.

x: All three statements are correct: the WTO was formed on 1 January 1995, the Uruguay Round was the eighth GATT round, and the Dunkel Draft belonged to it.

st.2: India destroyed its declared chemical-weapon stockpile by 2015.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: India finished destroying its stockpile in 2009. Statement 4 is wrong: the OPCW's organs are the Conference of States Parties, the Executive Council and the Technical Secretariat; a Board of Governors belongs to the IAEA.

st.1: The word 'secular' was added to the Preamble by the 44th Amendment, 1978.
st.3: Articles 29-30 guarantee freedom of religion.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: 'secular' was added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976. Statement 2 is wrong: Indian secularism means equal respect and principled distance, not complete separation. Statement 3 is wrong: freedom of religion is in Articles 25-28 (29-30 are cultural and educational rights).

st.3: The Viceroy's power to issue ordinances dates from the Indian Councils Act, 1861.

x: All three statements are correct: the 1919 Act made the central legislature bicameral, the 1935 Act gave six provinces bicameral legislatures, and the ordinance power dates from the 1861 Act.

st.1: Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse was borrowed from the USA.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse came from Australia. Statement 2 is wrong: the Concurrent List also came from Australia.

st.3: Under Article 35, both Parliament and the State Legislatures can legislate on Articles 16(3), 32(3), 33 and 34.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: 'martial law' is not defined in the Constitution. Statement 3 is wrong: under Article 35 only Parliament can legislate on these matters.

st.2: The POCSO Act protects all children, boys and girls alike.

x: All three statements are correct: POCSO came into force on 14 November 2012, it is gender-neutral, and the 2018 Ordinance allowed the death penalty for rape of a girl below 12.

st.1: It upheld the 103rd Amendment by a 4:1 majority.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 103rd Amendment was upheld by 3:2. Statement 2 is wrong: the Court held that the 50% ceiling does not apply to EWS reservation.

st.1: In 1956 Bombay State was divided into Maharashtra and Gujarat.
st.2: Himachal Pradesh was carved out of Punjab by the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Bombay State was divided in 1960. Statement 2 is wrong: the 1966 Act carved out Haryana (Himachal only received hill areas). Statement 4 is wrong: Telangana was formed on 2 June 2014.

st.4: At most 30 starred questions are listed a day for oral answer.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: supplementary questions are allowed only on starred questions. Statement 4 is wrong: at most 20 starred questions are listed a day.

st.3: Since 2017 the Union Budget is presented on 1 February.

x: All three statements are correct: the Railway Budget was separated in 1924 after the Acworth Committee, Arun Jaitley presented the first merged budget on 1 February 2017, and the budget is now presented on 1 February.

st.3: Nominated members are also covered: they are disqualified if they join a party after six months.

x: All three statements are correct: the Tenth Schedule first gave parties constitutional recognition, applies to Legislative Councils, and covers nominated members who join a party after six months.

st.3: For lesser misconduct, the In-House Procedure (1999) was adopted after K. Veeraswami (1991).

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the address needs a majority of total membership and two-thirds of those present and voting. Statement 3 is wrong: the In-House Procedure followed C. Ravichandran Iyer (1995).

st.3: Special leave to appeal under Article 136 can be granted against a court or tribunal under the armed forces law.
st.2: The President may by order enlarge the criminal appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: only Parliament, by law, can enlarge it. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 136 excludes armed forces courts and tribunals. Statement 4 is wrong: an appeal lies as of right when a High Court reverses an acquittal and sentences the accused to death.

st.2: The appointment of an acting judge comes to an end when he attains the age of 65.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: an additional judge is appointed for up to two years. Statement 2 is wrong: High Court judges, acting ones included, retire at 62.

st.4: President's Rule can continue beyond one year only if a National Emergency is in operation or the Election Commission certifies the need, up to three years in all.
st.3: The 42nd Amendment replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' as a ground for National Emergency.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Financial Emergency is under Article 360. Statement 3 is wrong: the change was made by the 44th Amendment. Statement 4 is wrong: both conditions must hold – a National Emergency and the Election Commission's certificate.

st.1: Each consists of a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and five other members.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: each has three other members. Statement 2 is wrong: the term is fixed by the President by rule (three years), not five years.

st.1: It submitted 15 reports.

x: All three statements are correct: the Second ARC was set up on 31 August 2005 under Moily, V. Ramachandran later succeeded him, and it submitted 15 reports.

st.4: The UN Human Rights Prize is given by the UN Human Rights Council, usually every five years, since 1968.
st.3: Human Rights Watch is a Geneva-based NGO.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Amnesty won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977. Statement 3 is wrong: Human Rights Watch is based in New York. Statement 4 is wrong: the UN Human Rights Prize is given by the UN General Assembly.

st.1: Jannat Hussain was the first State Chief Information Commissioner.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the first State CIC was C.D. Arha. Statement 3 is wrong: the second was Jannat Hussain; P. Ramesh Kumar came in 2020 in residuary AP.

st.1: It held public hearings (jan sunwais) in Maharashtra demanding access to muster rolls and bills.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the jan sunwais were held in Rajasthan. Statement 2 is wrong: MKSS was led by Aruna Roy, Nikhil Dey and Shanker Singh, not Medha Patkar.

st.2: It was not written into the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

x: All three statements are correct: Special Category Status was promised in Parliament by Manmohan Singh, was not written into the 2014 Act, and means 90% central funding of CSS.

st.3: It has met only 11 times, the last in July 2016.

x: All three statements are correct: the Council was set up on 28 May 1990, meets in camera and decides by consensus, and has met only 11 times.

st.3: The 131st Amendment Bill on Lok Sabha expansion was defeated, sharpening the North–South debate.

x: All three statements are correct: Ladakh was offered Article 371 safeguards, the FNTA covers 46 subjects, and the 131st Amendment Bill was defeated, sharpening the North–South debate.

st.3: Amit Shah was BJP president from 2014 to January 2020.

x: All three statements are correct: Nitin Nabin was elected unopposed in January 2026, Kharge has led the INC since October 2022, and Amit Shah was BJP president from 2014 to 2020.

st.2: A new party must apply for registration within 30 days of its formation.

x: All three statements are correct: both registration and recognition are done by the ECI, the application is due within 30 days, and the constitution must pledge allegiance to socialism, secularism and democracy.

st.1: The concept of Gram Swaraj was conceived by Mahatma Gandhi.

x: All three statements are correct: Gram Swaraj was Gandhi's idea, the RGSA builds PRI governance capacity, and its funding is 60:40 (90:10 for NE and hill States).

st.3: In Arunachal Pradesh only the reservation for Scheduled Tribes does not apply.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: in Arunachal Pradesh it is the SC reservation that does not apply (no SC population). Statement 4 is wrong: Part IX reached Jammu and Kashmir only after the 2019 reorganisation.

st.3: The law on all matters relating to Panchayat elections is made by the State Legislature.

x: All three statements are correct: the State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor, is removable only like a High Court judge, and Panchayat election law is made by the State Legislature.

st.2: Articles 330A and 332A reserve seats for women in the Lok Sabha and the State Legislative Assemblies.

x: All three statements are correct: Articles 325-326 give women equal franchise, Articles 330A and 332A (106th Amendment) reserve seats for women, and women's groups want the Census-delimitation condition removed.

st.4: The Municipal Commissioner is the chief executive, appointed by the Mayor.
st.1: Areas for Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils and Municipal Corporations are specified by the President by public notification.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the areas are specified by the Governor. Statement 3 is wrong: the council is headed by the Mayor. Statement 4 is wrong: the Commissioner is appointed by the State Government.

st.1: The Industrial, MSME, Electronics and Food Processing 4.0 policies were notified on 26 January 2025.
st.4: The Data Center Policy 4.0 was notified in March 2025.
st.3: The IT & GCC Policy 4.0 was issued on 12 December 2024; LIFT stands for Logistics Incentive for Tech Hubs.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: these policies were notified on 26 October 2024. Statement 2 is wrong: Electronics Manufacturing 4.0 is G.O.Ms.70 (G.O.Ms.71 is Food Processing). Statement 3 is wrong: LIFT stands for Land Incentive for Tech Hubs. Statement 4 is wrong: the Data Center Policy 4.0 came in November 2024.

st.2: The foundation stone of Amaravati was laid on 22 October 2015 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

x: All three statements are correct: AP was bifurcated on 2 June 2014 with the APCRDA Act passed that year, Modi laid the foundation stone on 22 October 2015, and Phase I is funded by the World Bank and ADB.

st.3: The ordinance was replaced by the Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act, 2015.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the ordinance placed ULIPs under IRDA, not SEBI. Statement 3 is wrong: the ordinance was replaced by the Securities and Insurance Laws (Amendment and Validation) Act, 2010.

st.4: Its Blue Economy target is US$50 billion by 2035.
st.1: Its coastline of about 1,053 km is the third longest among all Indian States and Union Territories.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: AP's coastline is the third longest among States; the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (a UT) also has a longer one. Statement 3 is wrong: the target is 4 greenfield ports and 11 fishing harbours. Statement 4 is wrong: the Blue Economy target is US$20 billion by 2035.

st.2: It had 166 members as of April 2026; Liberia became the 164th member in July 2016.
st.4: It came into being on 1 January 1996.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 164th member (July 2016) was Afghanistan. Statement 3 is wrong: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is the seventh Director-General. Statement 4 is wrong: the WTO came into being on 1 January 1995.

st.1: Agricultural labourers (14.4 crore) were still outnumbered by cultivators.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: in 2011 agricultural labourers (14.4 crore) outnumbered cultivators for the first time. Statement 2 is wrong: cultivators fell from 12.7 crore in 2001 to 11.9 crore in 2011.

st.3: The final child sex ratio (0-6 years) was 918.

x: All three statements are correct: the final sex ratio was 943, rural (949) exceeded urban (929), and the final child sex ratio was 918 (provisional 914).

st.1: Credit Linked Subsidy (CLSS) is a Centrally Sponsored vertical.
st.4: PMAY-U 2.0 (2024) aims at 2 crore more urban houses.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: CLSS is a Central Sector vertical. Statement 3 is wrong: In-situ Slum Redevelopment was dropped in PMAY-U 2.0. Statement 4 is wrong: PMAY-U 2.0 aims at 1 crore houses.

st.2: The Economic Survey 2022-23 projected real GDP growth of 7.5% for 2023-24.
st.3: The Economic Survey 2021-22 called for the State 'letting go'.

x: Statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: real GDP grew 8.2% in FY24. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2022-23 Survey projected 6.5%. Statement 3 is wrong: the call for the State 'letting go' came in the Economic Survey 2023-24.

st.4: Since 2021-22 it is presented in two volumes with a statistical appendix.
st.3: The first Survey was for 1950-51, and it has been presented separately from the Budget since 1974.
st.1: It is prepared by the Economic Division of the Department of Expenditure under the Chief Economic Adviser.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: it is prepared in the Department of Economic Affairs. Statement 2 is wrong: presenting it is a convention, not a constitutional duty under Article 112. Statement 3 is wrong: it has been separate from the Budget since 1964. Statement 4 is wrong: since 2021-22 it is a single volume with a statistical appendix.

st.2: The National Manufacturing Policy aimed to create 100 million jobs.

x: All three statements are correct: the NMP (2011) aimed at 25% of GDP and 100 million jobs by 2022, and Make in India was launched on 25 September 2014.

st.2: Construction was the fastest-growing sub-sector within industry (14.18%).

x: All three statements are correct: fishing and aquaculture led agriculture (17.69%), construction led industry (14.18%), and public administration grew least (0.05%).

st.1: Manufacturing employs only about 21.4% of workers (2023-24).

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: manufacturing employs only about 11.4% of workers. Statement 2 is wrong: agriculture is the largest employer; MSMEs come second.

st.1: Green Revolution HYV crops needed less irrigation than traditional varieties.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: HYV crops needed more irrigation, which depleted the water table. Statement 4 is wrong: groundwater depletion is caused mainly by over-extraction for irrigation, not brick-making.

st.3: Neither frictional nor structural unemployment can exist at full employment.
st.1: Educated unemployment in India is predominantly rural.
st.4: Seasonal and disguised unemployment are mainly urban.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: educated unemployment is mainly urban. Statement 2 is wrong: PLFS open unemployment is higher in urban areas. Statement 3 is wrong: frictional and structural unemployment can exist even at full employment. Statement 4 is wrong: seasonal and disguised unemployment are mainly rural.

st.2: A fixed five-year tenure and qualifications were prescribed for the Deputy Chairman and members of the Planning Commission.
st.1: The Planning Commission was set up by an Act of Parliament to prepare a common plan for the country.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Planning Commission was set up by an executive (Cabinet) resolution in 1950. Statement 2 is wrong: no fixed tenure or qualifications were prescribed. Statement 3 is wrong: UIDAI now functions under the Ministry of Electronics and IT.

st.2: Under the Proportional Reserve System followed till 1956, half of the assets had to be in gold or sterling securities.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: two-fifths (40%) had to be in gold or sterling. Statement 3 is wrong: the ₹515 crore reserve was ₹400 crore in foreign securities and ₹115 crore in gold.

st.1: The target is set once every five years and notified in the Official Gazette.

x: All three statements are correct: the target is set every five years, is defined by headline CPI-Combined, and was retained at 4% ±2% for 2026-31.

st.1: Swadesh Darshan and PRASHAD were launched in 2016-17.
st.2: India ranked 29th of 119 countries in the Travel & Tourism Development Index 2024.

x: Statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: both schemes were launched in 2014-15. Statement 2 is wrong: India ranked 39th. Statement 3 is wrong: Vision 2047 aims at 100 million foreign tourist arrivals, not 10 million.

st.3: A wholly owned subsidiary of a foreign bank needs a minimum capital of ₹500 crore.

x: All three statements are correct: scheduled banks are in the Second Schedule with ₹5 lakh minimum, DICGC was formed in 1978, and a foreign bank's WOS needs ₹500 crore.

st.4: Oriental Bank of Commerce and United Bank of India were merged into Bank of Baroda.
st.2: Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank were merged into Indian Bank.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Andhra and Corporation Banks went into Union Bank of India. Statement 3 is wrong: Allahabad Bank went into Indian Bank. Statement 4 is wrong: OBC and United Bank went into Punjab National Bank.

st.3: Of the ₹2.11 lakh crore recapitalisation of October 2017, ₹58,000 crore came through recapitalisation bonds.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 4Rs are Recognition, Resolution, Recapitalisation and Reforms. Statement 3 is wrong: ₹1.35 lakh crore came through recapitalisation bonds (about ₹58,000 crore was to come from the market).

st.1: EASE (Enhanced Access and Service Excellence) was launched in 2017 for both public and private sector banks.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: EASE is for public sector banks only. Statement 2 is wrong: EASE is run by the IBA's EASE Steering Committee, not a board of heads of financial institutions.

st.3: Total subsidies are about 18.5% of Union expenditure in 2026-27.
st.4: Under fertiliser DBT (2018), subsidy is released to companies when the fertiliser is dispatched from the plant.
st.1: The major subsidy heads are food, fertiliser and power.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the major heads are food, fertiliser and petroleum (LPG). Statement 2 is wrong: urea is the largest fertiliser subsidy item. Statement 3 is wrong: subsidies are about 8.5% of Union expenditure. Statement 4 is wrong: under DBT the subsidy is released only after the retail sale is recorded on PoS machines with Aadhaar authentication.

st.3: Budget 2026-27 reduced it to 12% and made it a final tax.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Budget 2026-27 set MAT at 14%. Statement 4 is wrong: no new MAT credit is allowed after 1 April 2026.

st.2: The Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers was set up in 2000, with Sushil Kumar Modi as its first chair.
st.1: GST was first proposed under the Narasimha Rao government.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: GST was first proposed under the Vajpayee government. Statement 2 is wrong: the Empowered Committee's first chair was Asim Dasgupta. Statement 4 is wrong: the 115th Amendment Bill lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha.

st.3: The US dollar had the largest currency share (54.8%), followed by the Indian rupee.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: total external debt was about $778.2 billion and the US dollar had the largest share (54.8%). Note: the notes give the debt-to-GDP ratio as 20.8%, not 29.8% (29.8% is the rupee's share).

st.3: The Revamped PDS (1992) targeted BPL families across the country.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: buffer stocks were formally introduced in the Fourth Plan. Statement 3 is wrong: the RPDS targeted remote and backward blocks; BPL targeting came with the TPDS (1997).

st.1: The Centre-State sharing ratio is generally 75:25.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the general MIDH ratio is 60:40. Statement 3 is wrong: the general ratio is 60:40, not 50:50.

st.2: It has been compulsory for loanee farmers since 2020.
st.1: It replaced NAIS and MNAIS in 2018.
st.3: Under it, YES-TECH is used for weather data and WINDS for remote-sensing-based yield estimation.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: PMFBY replaced NAIS and MNAIS in 2016. Statement 2 is wrong: since 2020 it is voluntary for all farmers. Statement 3 is wrong: YES-TECH is for yield estimation and WINDS for weather data. Statement 4 is wrong: the Weather Based scheme continues as the Restructured WBCIS.

st.2: It was established on 12 July 1982, during the Sixth Five Year Plan.

x: All three statements are correct: NABARD's Act was passed in 1981, it was set up on 12 July 1982 in the Sixth Plan, and it is headquartered in Mumbai.

st.3: Under that policy, a project above ₹1,001 crore is 'Ultra-Mega'.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the export target is US$20 billion to US$40 billion. Statement 3 is wrong: the Ultra-Mega threshold is above ₹5,001 crore.

st.1: A buyer must pay a micro or small enterprise supplier within 60 days.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: payment is due within 45 days at most. Statement 2 is wrong: on delay the buyer pays compound interest at three times the RBI bank rate.

st.1: The LIC IPO, the biggest IPO till then, was listed on 17 May 2021.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: LIC was listed on 17 May 2022. Statement 2 is wrong: the BPCL strategic sale was called off in 2022.

st.1: They are India's largest merchandise export.
st.2: They widen the merchandise trade deficit.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: software services are India's largest services export, not a merchandise export. Statement 2 is wrong: their surplus helps offset the merchandise trade deficit.

st.3: NPIT 2012 aimed at making at least one e-literate person in every household.

x: All three statements are correct: MeitY became a ministry in 2016, and NPIT 2012 aimed at USD 200 billion software exports and one e-literate person per household.

st.3: At constant prices in 2024-25 the agriculture : industry : services split was about 42 : 28 : 30.
st.2: The share of agriculture in AP's GSDP is about half India's share.
st.4: Agriculture employs about 25.6% of AP's workers (SES 2024-25).

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: services form a smaller share of AP's economy than of India's. Statement 2 is wrong: agriculture's share in AP is about twice India's. Statement 3 is wrong: the split was about 30 : 28 : 42. Statement 4 is wrong: agriculture employs about 45.6% of AP's workers.

st.1: The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 package covers 7 backward districts – 3 in Rayalaseema and 4 in North Coastal Andhra.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 7 districts are 4 in Rayalaseema and 3 in North Coastal Andhra. Statement 2 is wrong: Nalgonda is in Telangana and is not covered.

st.2: AP received ₹3,200 crore of central relief for Cyclone Titli.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the central relief for Titli was ₹1,200 crore. Statement 3 is wrong: the Agriculture Budget was presented by Agriculture Minister K. Atchannaidu.

st.2: The AP High Court upheld tax revenue going to APSDC instead of the Consolidated Fund of the State.
st.1: It escrowed mining royalty to borrow from banks.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: APSDC escrowed liquor revenue. Statement 2 is wrong: the High Court questioned, not upheld, tax revenue bypassing the Consolidated Fund.

st.1: Over 240 corporations and institutions worth more than ₹39,000 crore remain undivided.
st.2: Unapportioned public debt of over ₹24,000 crore on AP's books widens its FRBM borrowing room.

x: Statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: over 140 corporations and institutions remain undivided. Statement 2 is wrong: the unapportioned debt cuts AP's FRBM borrowing room. Statement 3 is wrong: AP wants the population ratio and Telangana insists on location.

st.3: APTRANSCO implements APCNF.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the largest disbursement was for the VCIC, then Health Systems Strengthening. Statement 3 is wrong: APCNF is implemented by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha.

st.1: AP is second in fruits, with 15.6% of national horticulture output.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: AP is first in fruits. Statement 4 is wrong: AP ranks third after Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra.

st.3: India's stunting rate is cited as 29.3%.

x: All three statements are correct: the Survey stresses quality and outcomes, MMR is cited as 88 and stunting as 29.3%.

st.1: A zero-coupon bond is issued at a premium and pays no periodic interest.
st.2: New issues of Sovereign Gold Bonds continue every quarter.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: a zero-coupon bond is issued at a discount. Statement 2 is wrong: new issues of Sovereign Gold Bonds have been stopped.

st.4: In 2016 SEBI approved online platforms offering equity crowdfunding.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: arbitrage funds must keep at least 65% in equity. Statement 4 is wrong: in 2016 SEBI called such platforms unauthorised.

st.2: The Earth is an oblate spheroid, flattened at the poles and bulging at the Equator.

x: All three statements are correct: geoid means earth-shaped, the Earth is flattened at the poles, and the equatorial radius exceeds the polar by about 21 km.

st.3: Tripura
st.4: Rajasthan

x: The Tropic of Cancer crosses Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand and Tripura in that order from west to east (4, 2, 1, 3).

st.2: The White Rabbit protocol was developed by CERN.

x: All three statements are correct: the Jakkur White Rabbit network gives sub-nanosecond GPS-independent timing, the protocol was developed by CERN, and the 2026 IST Rules come into force 180 days after publication.

st.2: The Sun is vertically overhead at the Tropic of Cancer on 21 March and 23 September.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: at the equinoxes the Sun is overhead at the Equator. Statement 3 is wrong: the tilt does not change; day length varies because the tilted axis keeps a fixed direction as the Earth revolves.

st.3: The outer core is the main source of magma.
st.2: The asthenosphere, at about 100–200 km in the lower mantle, is weak, plastic and partly molten.
st.1: The lithosphere is rigid and lies entirely within the crust.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the lithosphere includes the crust and the uppermost mantle. Statement 2 is wrong: the asthenosphere is in the upper mantle. Statement 3 is wrong: the asthenosphere is the main source of magma. Statement 4 is wrong: the barysphere is the core (the mesosphere is the lower mantle).

st.3: Sulphur dioxide aerosols can warm the Earth for years, while ash falls back within weeks.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: lahars come mainly from steep stratovolcanoes, not shield volcanoes. Statement 3 is wrong: sulphate aerosols cool the Earth.

st.1: An uvala is formed by joined (coalesced) poljes.
st.3: A blind valley ends abruptly where its stream emerges as a spring.
st.4: Lapiaz (karren) is a flat, smooth limestone surface.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: an uvala is formed by coalesced dolines. Statement 2 is wrong: a polje is a large flat-floored depression; the small funnel is the doline. Statement 3 is wrong: a blind valley ends where its stream sinks into the limestone. Statement 4 is wrong: lapiaz is a grooved, ridged surface.

st.2: The Kiel Canal, linking the North Sea and the Baltic, is in Germany.

x: All three statements are correct: the Panama Canal uses locks, the Kiel Canal is in Germany, and the lock-free Suez Canal opened in 1869.

st.2: Kerala's 'red rain' was observed in 2001.

x: All three statements are correct: blood rain comes from dust or spores in raindrops, Kerala's red rain fell in 2001, and the 16th Finance Commission recommended notifying heatwaves and lightning.

st.4: A corona around the Sun or Moon is formed by refraction through ice crystals of thin clouds.
st.2: In a primary rainbow red appears on the inner side.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: in a primary rainbow red is on the outer side. Statement 3 is wrong: a secondary rainbow involves two internal reflections. Statement 4 is wrong: a corona is formed by diffraction by small water droplets (ice-crystal refraction gives a halo).

st.2: The Afridi are a Pashtun tribe of the Bolan Pass region.
st.1: The Ainu of Hokkaido and Sakhalin were traditionally pastoral nomads.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Ainu were traditionally hunters and fishermen. Statement 2 is wrong: the Afridi belong to the Khyber Pass region. Statement 3 is wrong: the Eskimo are the Inuit; the Sami are of northern Scandinavia.

st.3: The Sargasso Sea is bounded on the west by the Gulf Stream.

x: All three statements are correct: gyres turn clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere, and the Sargasso Sea is bounded by the Canary Current (east), the North Atlantic Drift (north) and the Gulf Stream (west).

st.3: The Trans-Himalaya was formed before the Himalayas.

x: All three statements are correct: Manasarovar lies near the Kailash Range (the Ladakh Range's continuation in Tibet), the Ladakh Plateau is India's highest, and the Trans-Himalaya is older than the Himalayas.

st.3: It extends from Mangaluru to Kanyakumari.

x: All three statements are correct: the Malabar coast has kayals (backwaters) and teris (dunes) and runs from Mangaluru to Kanyakumari (Goa to Mangaluru is the Kanara coast).

st.3: In the 28-district set, Kurnool has the most mandals (40).
st.2: After 2014, Anantapur district had the most mandals (66), ahead of Chittoor.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Chittoor had the most mandals (66), ahead of Anantapur. Statement 3 is wrong: YSR Kadapa has the most mandals (40). Statement 4 is wrong: AP now has about 688 mandals, not 588.

st.4: The Disaster Management Act was enacted in 2004.
st.2: Chronically drought-prone areas receive less than 750 mm of rain and cover about 60% of it.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: chronically drought-prone areas cover about 33% of the cultivable land. Statement 3 is wrong: the IMD's all-India drought year needs a deficiency of more than 10% (with over 20% of the area affected). Statement 4 is wrong: the Act was enacted in 2005.

st.2: Rudraprayag is the confluence of the Alaknanda and the Pindar.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Karnaprayag is the confluence of the Alaknanda and the Pindar. Statement 2 is wrong: Rudraprayag is the confluence of the Alaknanda and the Mandakini.

st.2: INCOIS has been an autonomous body under ISRO since 1999.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: INCOIS is an autonomous body of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, not ISRO. Statement 4 is wrong: the tsunami warning system is run by INCOIS, Hyderabad, not the IMD.

st.1: China refines about 70% of the world's strategic minerals.

x: All three statements are correct: China refines about 70% of strategic minerals, Project Vault is a $12 billion stockpile, and the PM warned against weaponising critical minerals at the 18th BRICS Summit.

st.4: Rajasthan has the largest limestone reserves in India.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: AP is third in limestone production, after Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh. Statement 4 is wrong: Karnataka has the largest reserves (Rajasthan leads production).

st.3: The AP Mineral Development Corporation (APMDC) was incorporated in 1961.

x: All three statements are correct: AP holds about 30.4% of India's beach-sand minerals and 18.23 lakh carats of diamond resources, and APMDC was incorporated in 1961.

st.1: Russia has the largest proved natural-gas reserves in the world.

x: All three statements are correct: Russia has the largest proved gas reserves, the USA is the largest gas producer, and Venezuela has the largest proved oil reserves.

st.4: Drip and sprinkler irrigation cover about 32 per cent of the irrigated area.
st.2: India's cropping intensity in 2021-22 was 135.4 per cent.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: cropping intensity was 155.4%. Statement 3 is wrong: about 56% of net sown area is irrigated. Statement 4 is wrong: drip and sprinkler cover only about 12%.

st.2: Annadatha Sukhibhava is a State top-up to PM-KUSUM.
st.1: Andhra Pradesh has nine agro-climatic zones.
st.4: There are 16,606 Rythu Seva Kendralu in AP.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: AP has six agro-climatic zones. Statement 2 is wrong: Annadatha Sukhibhava tops up PM-KISAN. Statement 3 is wrong: RSKs were earlier called Rythu Bharosa Kendralu. Statement 4 is wrong: there are 10,606 RSKs.

st.3: Market-based industries locate near consumers because their products are weight-gaining or perishable.

x: All three statements are correct: water access is a location factor, aluminium is power-oriented, and market-based industries make weight-gaining or perishable goods.

st.2: Green hydrogen is an example of a sunrise industry.

x: All three statements are correct: diamond polishing and software are footloose, green hydrogen is a sunrise industry, and 'gold collar' refers to the quinary sector.

st.1: The India–UAE CEPA (2020) gave 90% duty-free access, and exports rose 12% in its first year.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the India–UAE CEPA came in 2022. Statement 3 is wrong: the India–UK CETA came into force on 15 July 2026, not in 2025.

st.2: Vizhinjam in Tamil Nadu is India's first deep-water transshipment port.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Vizhinjam is in Kerala. Statement 4 is wrong: Dahej is a non-major port.

st.3: India is the 7th largest services exporter, with a 4.3% share in 2024.

x: All three statements are correct: services are over half of GVA and the top FDI recipient, employ about 62% of urban workers, and India is the 7th largest services exporter (4.3%).

st.1: It is prepared by NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI, using 3 dimensions and 10 indicators.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the national MPI uses 12 indicators. Statement 2 is wrong: AP's MPI fell to 0.025. Statement 4 is wrong: West Godavari, not Guntur, has the lowest multidimensional poverty.

st.2: Buddhists became eligible for SC status in 1956.
st.1: Sikhs became eligible for SC status in 1990.
st.4: 79 Lok Sabha seats are reserved for SCs after the 2008 delimitation.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Sikhs became eligible in 1956. Statement 2 is wrong: Buddhists became eligible in 1990. Statement 3 is wrong: Jains are not eligible for SC status. Statement 4 is wrong: 84 seats are reserved for SCs (79 was the earlier figure).

st.2: The World Bank (2010) estimated that 65.3% of Indians lived in 'urban-like' areas.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the World Bank figure was 55.3%. Statement 3 is wrong: the EAC-PM's 63% estimate used satellite data.

st.3: Living root bridges are found in the Mishmi hills of Arunachal Pradesh.
st.1: Longpi pottery is associated with the Ao Naga.

x: Statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Longpi pottery belongs to the Tangkhul Naga. Statement 2 is wrong: the last head-hunters were the Konyak Naga. Statement 3 is wrong: living root bridges are in the Khasi and Jaintia hills of Meghalaya.

st.3: In November 2018, Odisha released bilingual dictionaries of 21 tribal languages.

x: All three statements are correct: Adi Vaani was launched under the Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan, first covers Bhili, Gondi, Mundari and Santali, and Odisha released 21 tribal dictionaries in 2018.

st.3: As per PLFS 2023-24, the tertiary sector employs about 31.6% of AP's workers.

x: All three statements are correct: the tertiary share of India's GVA was 52.9%, AP's primary share about 33%, and services employ about 31.6% of AP's workers.

st.1: According to GCRMN 2026, major disturbances to reefs now come every 10–12 years.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: GCRMN 2026 says major disturbances now come every 4–6 years. Statement 3 is wrong: the Andaman bleaching was linked to about a 2°C rise.

st.1: Black carbon, commonly called soot, is a long-lived greenhouse gas.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: black carbon is a short-lived climate pollutant (an aerosol, not a long-lived gas). Statement 2 is wrong: tropospheric ozone is a secondary pollutant formed from precursors, not emitted directly.

st.2: Solar irradiance (sunspot activity) is not one of the Milankovitch factors.

x: All three statements are correct: Milankovitch gave the astronomical theory in the 1920s, his factors are orbital (eccentricity, tilt, precession) not sunspots, and satellites since 1978 show no net rise in solar output.

st.3: ISRO functions under the Department of Atomic Energy.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: CSIR functions under the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research. Statement 3 is wrong: ISRO functions under the Department of Space.

st.3: Each student selected under INSPIRE-MANAK gets ₹25,000.
st.2: MANAK stands for Million Minds Advancing National Ambition and Knowledge.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: MANAK is Million Minds Augmenting National Aspiration and Knowledge. Statement 3 is wrong: each MANAK awardee gets ₹10,000. Statement 4 is wrong: about 65% of the 2025 fellowships went to women.

st.2: The National Mission for Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem covers 12 thematic areas.

x: All three statements are correct: the Solar Mission began on 11 January 2010 with 100 GW by 2022, NMSHE covers 12 thematic areas, and the Green India Mission was approved on 20 February 2014.

st.3: Tungsten is called the 'metal of the future'.
st.1: Graphene is a one-atom-thick sheet of carbon, linked to the 1996 Nobel Prize.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: graphene is linked to the 2010 Nobel Prize (1996 was for fullerenes). Statement 3 is wrong: titanium is the 'metal of the future'. Statement 4 is wrong: Bhabha Kavach uses BARC technology, not DRDO's.

st.1: Passive RFID tags have their own battery.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: active tags, not passive ones, have their own battery. Statement 2 is wrong: passive tags have a shorter range than active tags.

st.2: The Chairman of ISRO is also the Secretary, Department of Space and the Chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission.
st.1: The Department of Space reports to the Ministry of Science and Technology.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Department of Space reports directly to the Prime Minister. Statement 2 is wrong: the ISRO Chairman heads the Space Commission, not the Atomic Energy Commission. Statement 3 is wrong: Dr V. Narayanan is the 11th Chairman and succeeded S. Somanath.

st.3: Soil moisture is best measured from space by optical (visible-band) sensors.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Resourcesat and Oceansat are passive sensors. Statement 3 is wrong: soil moisture is best measured by microwave or SAR sensors.

st.2: States must request satellite data from NRSC during disasters.

x: All three statements are correct: the DMSP uses INSAT and IRS satellites, States must request data from NRSC, and the INSAT Disaster Warning System uses C-band uplink and S-band downlink from Chennai.

st.3: From 1 June 2026, the Chief of Defence Staff holds additional charge as DRDO Chairman.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Satheesh Reddy is a native of Nellore district. Statement 3 is wrong: the additional charge went to Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh, not the CDS.

st.2: 'Barak' means 'lightning' in Hebrew.

x: All three statements are correct: Barak-1 was first deployed on INS Virat, 'Barak' means lightning, and Kinzhal is Russia's air-launched hypersonic missile.

st.3: Digital payments grew at about 41% CAGR from 2017-18 to 2024-25.

x: All three statements are correct: UPI had about 85% of digital payment volume and 49% of world real-time payments, and digital payments grew at about 41% CAGR.

st.2: Australia has the world's largest uranium reserves.

x: All three statements are correct: NPCIL holds equity in BHAVINI, Australia has the largest uranium reserves, and Kazakhstan supplies about 80% of India's uranium imports.

st.1: India is the 2nd-largest producer and consumer of electricity in the world.
st.3: Per capita electricity consumption was 1,960 kWh in 2024-25.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: India is the 3rd-largest producer and consumer. Statement 3 is wrong: per capita consumption was 1,460 kWh. Statement 4 is wrong: NITI expects coal's share to fall to about 6–10% by 2070.

st.1: Di-Methyl Ether (DME) is formed from two methanol molecules by adding one water molecule.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: DME is formed by removing one water molecule. Statement 3 is wrong: M15 has 15% methanol in petrol, not diesel.

st.2: Unlike wind and biomass, it is not stored solar energy.

x: All three statements are correct: geothermal heat comes mostly from radioactive decay, it is not stored solar energy, and it can give 24x7 baseload power.

st.1: It crossed 50 GW in March 2024.
st.2: In January 2026 it was about 55 GW, about 20.6% of India's installed capacity.

x: Statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: wind crossed 50 GW in March 2025. Statement 2 is wrong: 55 GW was about 10.6% of capacity. Statement 3 is wrong: solar is India's largest renewable source; wind is second.

st.2: APSECM is mainly responsible for energy conservation.

x: All three statements are correct: NREDCAP is the RE nodal agency and the nodal agency for the 2023 Green Hydrogen policy, and APSECM handles energy conservation.

st.1: India's PSP potential of about 267 GW includes about 58 GW on-stream and 209 GW off-stream.

x: All three statements are correct: of India's 267 GW PSP potential about 58 GW is on-stream and 209 GW off-stream, installed capacity is only about 7 GW, and AP's potential is about 42,020 MW.

st.1: The hoolock gibbon of the Western Ghats is India's only ape.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the hoolock gibbon is found in North-East India, not the Western Ghats. Statement 2 is wrong: the red panda occurs in the Eastern Himalaya.

st.1: Bioremediation is the search in nature for commercially valuable compounds and genes.
st.2: The Traditional Knowledge Digital Library was set up in 2001 by ICAR and AYUSH.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: that search is bioprospecting (bioremediation is cleaning pollution with organisms). Statement 2 is wrong: the TKDL was set up by CSIR and AYUSH. Statement 4 is wrong: ABS was made operational by the Nagoya Protocol (2010).

st.1: The Net Zero Portal for voluntary net-zero disclosure was launched by NITI Aayog on 16 September 2026.
st.3: The India–Japan Joint Crediting Mechanism comes under Article 6.4 of the Paris Agreement.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Net Zero Portal was launched by the MoEFCC. Statement 2 is wrong: the UK CBAM starts on 1 January 2027. Statement 3 is wrong: the JCM comes under Article 6.2.

st.3: A CAG audit found forest quality improved on 1.1 million ha against a target of 1.4 million ha.
st.4: The National Afforestation Programme works through Biodiversity Management Committees at the village level.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the CAG found improvement on only 0.11 million ha. Statement 4 is wrong: the NAP works through Joint Forest Management Committees.

st.1: Under the 2024 amendment, makers of biodegradable plastics need certification from the CPCB.

x: All three statements are correct: biodegradable-plastic makers need CPCB certification, the rigid packaging recycled-content target rises from 30% to 60%, and EPR shortfalls can be carried forward up to three years.

st.2: The PRANA portal was launched in 2021 to monitor NCAP.

x: All three statements are correct: PRANA is the Portal for Regulation of Air-pollution in Non-Attainment cities, launched in September 2021, and the CPCB coordinates NCAP with the SPCBs.

st.4: Hydrogen on burning gives water and carbon dioxide.
st.3: CNG and LPG release more particulate matter than diesel.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: CNG and LPG burn cleaner, with far less particulate matter than diesel. Statement 4 is wrong: hydrogen contains no carbon, so burning it gives only water.

st.3: The 12 principles of green chemistry were given by Paul Anastas and John Warner in 1991.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: cleaner production is preventive, not end-of-pipe. Statement 3 is wrong: Anastas and Warner gave the 12 principles in 1998.

st.1: Ozone is formed when infrared radiation splits molecular oxygen.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: ozone forms when ultraviolet radiation splits molecular oxygen. Statement 3 is wrong: an ozone hole is identified below 220 Dobson Units.

st.3: In 2025, more than 50% of the oceans had marine heatwaves.
st.1: Cyclones over the Arabian Sea rose by about 25% during 2001-2019.
st.2: Marine heatwaves can raise cyclone winds by up to 12% and rain by up to 20%.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Arabian Sea cyclones rose about 52%. Statement 2 is wrong: marine heatwaves raise winds up to 20% and rain up to 12%. Statement 3 is wrong: more than 90% of the oceans had marine heatwaves. Statement 4 is wrong: cyclones are more frequent in the Bay of Bengal.

st.4: Diphtheria forms a false membrane in the throat and spreads mainly through contaminated water.
st.2: Leprosy mainly affects the lungs and the intestines.
st.1: Tuberculosis, caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, is airborne and detected by the Widal test.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: TB is detected by the Mantoux test (Widal is for typhoid). Statement 2 is wrong: leprosy mainly affects the skin and peripheral nerves. Statement 3 is wrong: Mycobacterium leprae causes leprosy; diphtheria is caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae. Statement 4 is wrong: diphtheria spreads by respiratory droplets.

st.1: Nafithromycin (Miqnaf), India's first indigenous fluoroquinolone, was developed by Wockhardt with BIRAC.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Nafithromycin is a macrolide. Statement 4 is wrong: the Red Line marks prescription-only antibiotics, not all OTC medicines.

st.3: The number 19 in 'COVID-19' refers to 2019, the year it emerged.

x: All three statements are correct: SARS-CoV-2 was identified in Wuhan in December 2019, enters cells via ACE2 (pangolin suspected as intermediate host), and the 19 refers to 2019.

st.2: The Centre:State funding ratio is 60:40, and 90:10 for the North-Eastern and Himalayan States.

x: All three statements are correct: NRHM came in 2005 and NUHM in 2013, funding is 60:40 (90:10 for NE and Himalayan States), and the ASHA links households to the health system with the ANM.

st.2: COBOL is mainly used for business data processing.

x: All three statements are correct: FORTRAN (IBM, 1957) was the first high-level language, COBOL is for business data processing, and PROLOG and LISP are AI languages.

st.3: The rules under the Online Gaming Act took effect on 1 January 2026.
